"The DNS window shows DNS traffic statistical data" ... "DNS returns different codes. The list of these codes is available in the DNS statistics window."

This is a long way to say that "DNS statistics exist". It does not describe what they are or how they could be used.
@moshekaplan would you explain it to me or provide a draft that I can convert it into docs? thanks
simplified.

It's not just (response) codes, there are also statistics about request-response and counters for various aggregations.

The documentation could suggest how to use or interpret these statistics:
- The total count of DNS messages is displayed.
- Each message is further broken down into some groups, namely by request types (opcodes), response code (rcode),  query type, and more.

Consider this: if you were a reader, would the documentation help you getting additional insight in how to use this? If not, what questions would you like to be answered?

It should include at least the level of detail Peter wrote.

Here's a starting place:
```
Domain Name System (DNS) associates information, like IP addresses, with domain names.
Wireshark's DNS statistics break down the DNS statistics into groups, namely by request
types (opcodes), response code (rcode), query type (requested record type), Service Stats
(timing data), and Query Stats (length of record queried, number of labels, and length of payload).

.DNS statistics window
image::wsug_graphics/ws-dns.png[{screenshot-attrs}]

These statistics can be useful for quickly examining the health of a DNS service or other investigations. Here are a few possible examples:
* If DNS queries have a long request-response time or if there are many unanswered queries, the DNS server might have issues.
* DNS requests with abnormally large requests and responses might be indicative of DNS tunneling or command-and-control traffic.
* If there are an order of magnitude more DNS responses than requests and the responses are very large, it's possible that the target is being attacked with a DNS-based DDoS.
```

You can also see what @alagoutte wrote when he added the DNS statistics feature: https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/commit/696fcdba218c1c63537425149b63811ef8d9d73c#diff-152933d90149588c029c4e1ff6681c67ea657dc019531fa7a63ec2576f21da33

This page also gives an example of how DNS statistics can be used for troubleshooting:
https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/mastering-wireshark-2/9781788626521/97ec6764-6571-4cc3-ba54-96e0a1422639.xhtml

Here is an article explaining DNS tunneling:
https://www.varonis.com/blog/dns-tunneling/

Here is an article on DNS Amplification attacks: 
https://web.archive.org/web/20101214074629/http://www.isotf.org/news/DNS-Amplification-Attacks.pdf
great, @moshekaplan ! thanks a lot for the examples! added them to the docs.
